Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- CNN wants to hear from viewers in both English and Russian for its weeklong focus on modern Russia. CNN Moscow Correspondent at Star City, the Russian cosmonaut training facility. Reflecting on Dmitry Medvedev's first year as president, and looking ahead to President Obama's first trip to the Kremlin in July, CNN delves beyond politics to profile the many facets of this vast land through an ambitious bi-lingual audience initiative and a wide-ranging week of programming. The audience initiative -- CNN's first with a Russian-language component -- complements an energetic mix of live reporting and interviews, feature and documentary programming, and cultural despatches running the gamut of sports to space travel, fashion to music, business to farming, as CNN travels the length of the country to bring viewers the Russia of today. CNN wants to hear from both Russian residents and worldwide viewers, in English or in Russian, what they think about Russia's role in the international community. Send us your comments via Sound Off below. or send your videos and pictures via iReport or to youtube.com/CNN. The best will be posted online to be read and watched by CNN.com Youtube audiences around the world, while English language contributions have the additional opportunity to feature on air in CNN's programming output. "Russia is making its voice heard far beyond its borders at a time when the global community has never been more interdependent," said Mike McCarthy, CNN International's vice president of coverage and feature programming. "We want our compelling interviews and reports to stand alongside the very best in audience commentary to provide a really lively insight into what contemporary Russia looks like at a time when its impact is being felt not just in politics but in a diverse array of other fields. We're also excited to offer an online outlet for the first time for Russian language audience feedback as well." The week of programming kicks off with a special travelogue documentary Eye on Russia: Moving Forward where CNN's Moscow-based Senior International Correspondent Matthew Chance rides the train from the Arctic north of Murmansk down to the southern climes of Sochi by way of St Petersburg and Moscow, to offer a diverse range of reports. He visits a Russian farm to look at the country's ambitions to be an agricultural superpower, checks out the Star City astronaut training center, meets with seven-foot boxing world champion-turned-movie star Nikolai Valuev and talks along the way with entrepreneurs and environmentalists working to make the city of Sochi home to green Olympics in 2014. CNN also catches up with famous faces like NHL hockey star Alexander Ovechkin, Russian Vogue editor in chief Aliona Doletskaya, A list model Natalia Vodianova, acclaimed conductor Valery Gergiev, the "Russian Madonna" singer Valeriya, and London-based Russian art collector Nonna Materkova to bring together an eclectic mix of Russians who have made it on the world stage. Additionally, there are reports on Russian communities around the world that have sprung up in places as different as Ashdod, Israel and Brighton Beach, New York. CNN is also live every night from a range of iconic Moscow locations as Chance gives his topical insights into a country increasingly at the center of international headlines, to complement a range of interviews with top Russian CEOs and industry leaders airing throughout CNN's prime time evening programming. From St Basil's Cathedral, the Kremlin, Christ the Saviour Cathedral and Manej Square, Chance gives us the latest on what makes the Russia of today, from domestic and foreign policy, to business, to culture. The Eye on series has travelled around the world visiting France, Russia, India, South Korea, China, South Africa, Brazil, Beirut and Poland.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a CNN-style press release announcing a weeklong “Eye on Russia” programming focus, including a bilingual English/Russian audience initiative, featured correspondents, planned segments, and notable Russian personalities.
counterfactuals.output:
**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

## CNN Announces Weeklong “Eye on Russia” Programming Focus

**New York, NY — [Date]** — CNN will present **“Eye on Russia,”** a weeklong, network-wide programming initiative examining Russia’s politics, society, culture, economy, and global influence through original reporting, expert analysis, and on-the-ground perspectives.

Airing across CNN platforms, the special coverage will bring viewers inside the forces shaping modern Russia and its relationship with the world — from the Kremlin and the war in Ukraine to Russian business, technology, arts, sports, and the lives of ordinary citizens navigating rapid change.

### Bilingual Audience Initiative: “Russia in Two Voices / Россия в двух голосах”

As part of the weeklong focus, CNN will launch a bilingual audience engagement feature, **“Russia in Two Voices / Россия в двух голосах,”** inviting English- and Russian-speaking audiences to submit questions, short video reflections, and story ideas about Russia’s role in the world today.

Selected submissions will be featured across CNN digital and social platforms, with key segments presented in both English and Russian. The initiative is designed to broaden the conversation and give audiences a direct opportunity to engage with CNN journalists, analysts, and regional experts.

### Featured Correspondents and Contributors

“Eye on Russia” will feature reporting and analysis from CNN’s global team, including:

- **Clarissa Ward**, Chief International Correspondent  
- **Matthew Chance**, Senior International Correspondent  
- **Christiane Amanpour**, Chief International Anchor  
- **Fred Pleitgen**, Senior International Correspondent  
- **Bianna Golodryga**, Anchor and Senior Global Affairs Analyst  
- **Fareed Zakaria**, Host of *Fareed Zakaria GPS*  
- **Nic Robertson**, International Diplomatic Editor  
- CNN national security, foreign policy, economics, and disinformation analysts

Coverage will originate from key international locations including Washington, London, Brussels, Kyiv, and the wider region, with additional reporting from correspondents and producers tracking Russian political, social, and economic developments.

### Planned Segments

Programming highlights will include:

**“Inside the Kremlin’s Calculus”**  
A detailed look at President Vladimir Putin’s political strategy, Russia’s security establishment, and the decision-making structures behind Moscow’s domestic and foreign policy.

**“Russia and the War in Ukraine”**  
CNN correspondents and military analysts examine the latest battlefield developments, the human cost of the war, and the diplomatic efforts shaping the conflict’s future.

**“The Sanctions Economy”**  
A report on how Western sanctions have affected Russian markets, consumers, energy exports, technology access, and the country’s long-term economic outlook.

**“The Information Front”**  
An investigation into state media, online propaganda, censorship, and the battle over narratives inside and outside Russia.

**“Young Russia”**  
A feature on young Russians confronting questions of identity, opportunity, emigration, patriotism, and political pressure.

**“Culture Under Pressure”**  
A look at Russian artists, writers, musicians, and filmmakers navigating censorship, exile, and the tension between cultural heritage and political reality.

**“Russia’s Global Reach”**  
An examination of Moscow’s influence in Africa, the Middle East, Asia, the Arctic, and cyberspace.

**“Voices from the Diaspora”**  
Russian journalists, activists, entrepreneurs, and families living abroad discuss exile, identity, and their hopes for Russia’s future.

### Notable Russian Personalities and Figures

The special programming will examine the roles and influence of prominent Russian figures, including:

- **Vladimir Putin**, President of Russia  
- **Sergey Lavrov**, Foreign Minister  
- **Alexei Navalny’s political movement and legacy**  
- **Mikhail Khodorkovsky**, former oil executive and Kremlin critic  
- **Elvira Nabiullina**, Governor of the Central Bank of Russia  
- **Yevgeny Prigozhin’s Wagner legacy** and the future of Russian private military networks  
- Russian cultural figures, independent journalists, opposition voices, and members of the Russian diaspora

CNN will also feature interviews and expert conversations with historians, economists, former diplomats, security analysts, and regional specialists to provide context and depth throughout the week.

### Across CNN Platforms

“Eye on Russia” will air across CNN’s television programming and will be supported by expanded coverage on CNN.com, CNN International, CNN Podcasts, CNN Digital Video, and social media platforms. Interactive timelines, explainers, archival footage, and audience-driven Q&A segments will accompany the broadcasts.

**“Russia remains one of the most consequential stories in the world,”** said a CNN spokesperson. **“With ‘Eye on Russia,’ CNN is bringing together its global reporting resources to help audiences understand not only the politics and power structures, but also the people, pressures, and history behind the headlines.”**

**“Eye on Russia” begins [Start Date] and continues through [End Date] across CNN platforms.**

For more information, visit **CNN.com/EyeOnRussia**.

**Media Contact:**  
CNN Communications  
press@cnn.com  
[Phone Number]

**New audience engagement effort invites Russian-speaking viewers worldwide to share questions, comments, and perspectives as CNN presents in-depth coverage of Russia’s politics, culture, economy, sports, space exploration, fashion, agriculture, and global influence.**

CNN today announced the launch of its first Russian-language viewer feedback initiative, created to coincide with a dedicated week of special programming examining contemporary Russia and its role in the world.

The initiative will invite Russian-speaking audiences to respond directly to CNN’s coverage, submit questions for journalists and analysts, and share personal perspectives on the issues shaping Russian society today. The effort is designed to broaden dialogue with viewers across Russia, neighboring countries, and the global Russian-speaking diaspora.

By offering Russian-language feedback opportunities, we hope to encourage a wider range of viewer participation and provide a platform for questions and viewpoints that might otherwise go unheard.”

The viewer feedback initiative will allow audiences to submit comments and questions in Russian, with selected responses potentially featured across CNN programming, digital platforms, and audience segments connected to the special coverage. Viewers will be encouraged to respond to specific themes raised during the week, including how Russia is changing, how it is viewed internationally, and how Russian citizens and Russian-speaking communities see their place in the world.

The special programming will include coverage across several key areas:

- **Politics and Power:** Analysis of Russia’s political landscape, governance, public opinion, and the country’s relationship with major world powers.  
- **Economy and Business:** Reporting on energy, trade, technology, sanctions, investment, consumer life, and Russia’s evolving economic priorities.  
- **Culture and Society:** Features on literature, film, music, media, language, identity, and the cultural forces shaping daily life.  
- **Sports:** Coverage of Russia’s athletic traditions, international competition, sports diplomacy, and the role of sport in national identity.  
- **Space Travel and Science:** Reports on Russia’s space legacy, current aerospace ambitions, scientific research, and cooperation and competition in orbit.  
- **Fashion and Design:** Segments on Russian designers, street style, luxury markets, traditional influences, and the global visibility of Russian fashion.  
- **Farming and Rural Life:** Stories on agriculture, food production, rural economies, climate challenges, and Russia’s role in global grain and commodity markets.  
- **Global Influence:** Examination of Russia’s diplomatic, military, cultural, technological, and informational reach across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and beyond.

The programming aims to move beyond headlines by looking at the complexity of Russian life and the country’s many connections to global events.

By opening a dedicated channel for Russian-language responses, CNN seeks to make its coverage more interactive and responsive to the questions audiences are asking.

Viewers will be able to take part by submitting feedback in Russian through CNN-designated digital channels during the programming week. Prompts connected to each day’s reporting will invite audiences to comment on specific topics, share experiences, or pose questions for CNN journalists and guests.

Selected viewer questions and comments may be incorporated into televised discussions, online features, social media posts, or follow-up reporting.

The special week of coverage and the accompanying Russian-language feedback initiative underscore CNN’s continued focus on international reporting, cross-cultural dialogue, and audience participation at a time when Russia remains one of the most consequential and closely watched countries in the world.
